name: Neck-Shoulder Tension (Moderate)
description: 4-phase program for moderate tension: Relaxation, Mobilization, Strengthening, Functional Training - adjusted dosage
pain_rule: Perform exercises at pain <= 3/10. Reduce load if tension increases. Slower progression than with mild tension.
evidence_base: Gross et al. (2015): Exercise for mechanical neck disorders
Jull et al. (2008): Cranio-cervical flexion training
Falla et al. (2012): Specific deep cervical flexor exercise
Ylinen et al. (2003): Active neck muscle training in chronic neck pain
progression_criteria: Phase 1 -> 2: 14 days, min. 4 sessions, tension noticeably reduced
Phase 2 -> 3: 14 days, min. 4 sessions, good mobility, pain <= 3/10
Phase 3 -> 4: 14 days, min. 4 sessions, strength built up, pain <= 3/10

phase_education.1:
**Phase 1: Relaxation & Pain Relief**

With moderate tension, your body needs a bit more time to recover. The focus is on gentle relaxation and careful mobilization. Take enough time for each exercise.

**Goal:** Gradually release tension without overloading.

**Strategy:**
- Longer breathing exercises for deeper relaxation
- Reduced repetitions with higher focus on quality
- Longer stretch positions for sustained tissue relaxation
- Stay in this phase for at least 14 days

**Scientific Basis:** With moderate tension, a longer relaxation phase shows better long-term results. Tissue adaptation takes time (Gross et al., 2015).
phase_education.2:
**Phase 2: Mobilization & Control**

The acute tension has eased. Now we gently build mobility and control. Intensity remains moderate.

**Goal:** Gradually improve mobility and neuromuscular control.

**Strategy:**
- Careful increase of hold times
- Reduced repetition count compared to the mild variant
- Focus on correct execution
- Gentler progressions with resistance band exercises

**Scientific Basis:** Gradual load progression is crucial for sustained improvement with moderate symptoms (Jull et al., 2008).
phase_education.3:
**Phase 3: Strengthening**

Your mobility has improved. Now we strengthen the muscles - with adjusted intensity and lighter weights.

**Goal:** Gradual strength building without overloading.

**Strategy:**
- Lighter weights than the mild variant
- Fewer repetitions, but more precise execution
- Isometric exercises at moderate intensity
- Reduce intensity if tension increases

**Scientific Basis:** With moderate symptoms, adjusted strengthening intensity leads to better compliance and comparable long-term results (Ylinen et al., 2003).
phase_education.4:
**Phase 4: Functional Integration**

You have made great progress! Now we integrate the gained strength into your daily life and build a sustainable maintenance program.

**Goal:** Long-term freedom from symptoms with an adapted maintenance program.

**Strategy:**
- Functional exercises with moderate load
- Regular workplace micro-breaks
- Self-massage as a daily routine
- Maintenance training 3x/week

**Scientific Basis:** An individually adapted maintenance program is the most important factor for long-term freedom from symptoms.

exercises.name: Diaphragmatic Breathing with Shoulder Relaxation
exercises.description: Seated or lying on your back. Place hands on your abdomen. Breathe deeply through the nose into the belly (4 sec), exhale slowly through the mouth (6 sec). With each exhale, consciously let the shoulders drop. Longer sessions for deeper relaxation.
exercises.phase_goal: Gently release tension and regain mobility

exercises.name: Chin Tuck
exercises.description: Sit upright, gaze straight ahead. Gently retract the chin, as if making a double chin. Lengthen the neck. Hold the position, then slowly release. Fewer repetitions but longer hold time.
exercises.phase_goal: Gently release tension and regain mobility

exercises.name: Gentle Cervical Mobility (4 Directions)
exercises.description: Sit upright. Slowly tilt the head forward, return. Then backward, return. Left side, return. Right side, return. Only to 75% of pain-free range. Slower and more careful than with mild tension.
exercises.phase_goal: Gently release tension and regain mobility

exercises.name: Upper Trapezius Stretch (Extended)
exercises.description: Sit upright. Right hand grips under the chair. Tilt head to the left, gently place left hand on the head (no pressure!). Longer stretch for better tissue relaxation. Hold 45 seconds, switch sides.
exercises.phase_goal: Gently release tension and regain mobility

exercises.name: Scapular Setting
exercises.description: Sit upright, arms hanging loosely. Gently draw the shoulder blades back and down together, without raising the shoulders. Hold the position. Fewer repetitions but more focused.
exercises.phase_goal: Gently release tension and regain mobility

exercises.name: Levator Scapulae Stretch (Extended)
exercises.description: Sit upright. Slightly rotate the head to the left, then tilt forward and down. Right hand grips under the chair. Feel the stretch at the right neck-shoulder junction. Hold 45 seconds for deeper tissue relaxation. Switch sides.
exercises.phase_goal: Gently release tension and regain mobility

exercises.name: CCF Endurance Progression
exercises.description: Lying on your back, head on a pillow. Slowly and deliberately tuck the chin. Carefully increase hold time to 8-12 seconds. Quality over duration - take a break immediately when control fades.

exercises.name: Prone Y/T/W Lifts
exercises.description: Lying face down on the floor. Alternately lift arms in Y-, T-, and W-position off the floor. Squeeze shoulder blades together, hold 2 seconds, lower. Fewer repetitions but more precise.

exercises.name: Wall Slides
exercises.description: Stand with your back against the wall. Place arms in 90-degree position against the wall. Slowly slide arms upward. Actively draw shoulder blades down. Reduced range of motion at the start is fine.

exercises.name: Thoracic Rotation (Open Book)
exercises.description: Side-lying, knees bent. Slowly open the top arm to the other side. Eyes follow the hand. Hold 3 seconds at end range, return. Do not rotate beyond the pain threshold.

exercises.name: Band Rows with Scapular Guidance
exercises.description: Attach resistance band in front of you. Grip the band, pull elbows back. Lighter resistance than with mild tension. Consciously perform scapular movement. Slowly return.

exercises.name: Side-Lying External Rotation
exercises.description: Side-lying, top arm at the body, elbow bent 90 degrees. Slowly rotate the forearm upward. Elbow stays at the body. Start without added weight. Only add 0.5 kg when pain-free execution is achieved.

exercises.name: Neck Flexor Endurance (Supine)
exercises.description: Lying on your back. Tuck the chin and lift the head slightly off the surface. Hold position. Shorter hold time than with mild tension. If trembling occurs, immediately lower.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Shoulder Shrugs (Light Weight)
exercises.description: Standing, hold light dumbbells (2-4 kg) at your sides. Raise shoulders upward for 3 seconds, briefly hold at the top, lower for 3 seconds in a controlled manner. Lighter weight than with mild tension.

exercises.name: Band Face Pulls (Light)
exercises.description: Attach resistance band at face height. Grip band with both hands, pull toward the ears. Lighter resistance. Squeeze shoulder blades together. Slowly return.

exercises.name: Prone I/Y/T without Weight
exercises.description: Lying face down. Lift arms in I-position, Y-position, and T-position off the floor. No added weight - only arm bodyweight. Actively squeeze shoulder blades together. Hold 2 seconds.

exercises.name: Isometric Neck Work (4 Directions)
exercises.description: Sit upright. Press hand against the head: front, back, left, right. Head holds position against hand resistance. 8 seconds per direction. More moderate pressure than with mild tension.

exercises.name: Wall Push-Up Plus
exercises.description: Standing against the wall (easier variant). Push-up against the wall, at the top push shoulder blades extra forward. Serratus activation with reduced load.

exercises.name: Light Overhead Press
exercises.description: Seated. Very light dumbbells (1-2 kg) or water bottles at shoulder height. Press up in a controlled manner. Slowly return. Keep core stable.

exercises.name: Rows with Thoracic Rotation
exercises.description: Single-arm band row: grip band, pull elbow back, then rotate thoracic spine toward the pulling side. Lighter resistance. Slow and controlled.
exercises.phase_goal: Long-term freedom from symptoms and prevention

exercises.name: Workplace Micro-Break (3-in-1)
exercises.description: At the desk: 1) Chin tuck (hold 5 sec), 2) Squeeze shoulder blades together (hold 5 sec), 3) Extend thoracic spine (hold 5 sec). Repeat every 45-60 minutes. More frequent breaks than with mild tension.
exercises.phase_goal: Long-term freedom from symptoms and prevention

exercises.name: Cervicoscapular Circuit (Adapted)
exercises.description: Adapted circuit training: 1) Chin tuck 8x, 2) Light shoulder shrugs 8x, 3) Band face pull 8x, 4) Wall slides 8x, 5) Thoracic rotation 6x per side. 45 sec rest between exercises. 2 rounds.
exercises.phase_goal: Long-term freedom from symptoms and prevention

exercises.name: Self-Massage Upper Trapezius & Suboccipital
exercises.description: With fingers or tennis ball: 1) Massage the upper trapezius along the shoulder-neck line (2 min), 2) Work the suboccipital muscles at the base of the skull with circular movements (2 min), 3) Gentle pressure on painful points (1 min). Daily routine.
exercises.phase_goal: Long-term freedom from symptoms and prevention

exercises.name: Maintenance Training (3x/Week)
exercises.description: Compact program: 1) Chin tuck 2x10, 2) Band face pull 2x10, 3) Light shoulder shrugs 2x10, 4) Wall slides 2x10, 5) Upper trapezius stretch 2x45s. Total duration approx. 15 minutes.
exercises.phase_goal: Long-term freedom from symptoms and prevention
